content: Is someone working on upstreaming the definitions of distribution, wnorm and HasWeakType, or have any comments on that? I am interested in it, so I am willing to do it or help

I think nobody is working on that yet, and upsteaming them would be great!
(cc @Leo Diedering, @Evgenia Karunus)

The first two maybe/probably have to be renamed before they will be accepted to Mathlib. For the first one I don't know a better name (e.g. Wikipedia just calls it the distribution function). For the second one I intentionally dropped the e in contrast to eLpNorm. The e signifies that it is ENNReal-valued, but I don't think there is really a desire to have a (NN)Real-valued version of it, so I personally think we can drop the e. That of course needs to be done only if there is a Zulip consensus that this is what we want.

Thank you for taking the lead on this!
I can imagine weakNorm (or eWeakNorm) might be better names for Mathlib.
I'm in vigorous agreement here - upstreaming this would be great, thanks a lot for starting this discussion!

Floris van Doorn said:

I think nobody is working on that yet, and upsteaming them would be great!
(cc Leo Diedering, Evgenia Karunus)

(I'm not working on it)

One thing we should think about before upstreaming wnorm and HasWeakType: do we actually want these in Mathlib, or do we only want carleson#MeasureTheory.eLorentzNorm and carleson#MeasureTheory.HasLorentzType, that generalize these notions?
Is this similar to the question of whether eLorentzNorm should generalize elpNorm? Given that they are just definitions and not defeq, perhaps it would be nice to have all of them?

It's definitely a similar question. I think the LpL^pLp norms are so much more ubiquitous than the Lorentz-norms, that we want them separately. I'm less convinced that this is also the case for the weak norm.
